Phase 7 bugalizer-revive (B0), impl r1. Commit ac28b09 on branch phase-7/bugalizer-revive-impl (off main at c6a720d, which already carries the approved plan and the tree cleanup). Full suite: 247 passed, 0 skipped @ ac28b09 (was 201; 46 new tests). No gatekeeper on this project, so that run is the one on the record.

What changed, where:
- models.py: LLMOverride (provider, model, api_key as SecretStr, key_ref max 128 charset [A-Za-z0-9._:/-]), AnalyzeRequest.llm, AnalyzeResponse.llm_source; IngestSource, SupabaseIngestConfig (extra=forbid; https URL with no userinfo/query/fragment; table identifier; credential_env ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$), validate_ingest_pair (single checkpoint, fixed non-echoing messages); ProjectCreate/Update/Response ingest fields; UsageAttribution + UsageSummary.attribution (additive; aggregate fields untouched per your plan note).
- api/reports.py analyze: override rules as HTTPException(422) with fixed detail strings (override needs tier cloud; key_ref needs api_key; key_ref must not equal the key). Override is passed as llm_override= kwarg on add_task only when it carries provider/model/key; otherwise the call shape is unchanged (existing assert_awaited_once_with(report_id) tests still hold). llm_source computed as request/project/global.
- pipeline/orchestrator.py: process_fix_proposal(report_id, llm_override=None) pass-through.
- pipeline/fix_proposer.py: _safe_error_text(exc, secrets) = '<Type>: <msg>' with each supplied secret and common key shapes (sk-, sk-ant-, Bearer) replaced by [redacted]; used for the deferred info line, the failure error line and the persisted analyses.result.error. Key unwrapped once in propose_fix into a local; request field wins per field over resolve_fix_llm; complete() gets api_key=request_key; token_usage_create gets key_source/key_ref. Classification untouched.
- main.py: RequestValidationError handler strips input and ctx project-wide; /health adds auth_enabled.
- api/projects.py: create validates the pair; PATCH loads the stored row, merges exclude_unset fields, null on either ingest field clears both, validates, then writes; ingest fields join the nullable set; _checked_ingest_pair converts ValueError to 422.
- db.py: schema + 4 ADD COLUMN migrations (token_usage ones guarded on table existence for the legacy-schema test); project_create/get/list/update handle ingest_config JSON; token_usage_create takes key_source/key_ref; token_usage_summary adds the attribution query.
- New: .github/workflows/ci.yml; scripts/windows/check-service.ps1. Docs: README + CLAUDE.md no test count (CLAUDE.md test map rewritten without counts), docs/deploy-windows.md section 6 one-liner, docs/decision_log.md entry for the two seams.

Verification (tests, 46 new): test_api.py: health auth_enabled true/false; validation handler drops input/ctx; four override 422 shapes each asserting the sentinel key is absent from the body; ingest matrix (pair round trip via POST/GET/list, defaults null, source-only, config-only, unknown source, extra secret field without echo, 4 bad URL shapes, 4 bad env names, bad table, config-only PATCH against stored source, config-only PATCH with no source, source-only PATCH, pair PATCH, null on either clears both, invalid PATCH leaves row unchanged). test_analysis_mode.py: override dispatch carries the LLMOverride kwarg and reports llm_source=request without echoing the key; no-override reports global then project; empty llm object is not a request source; local tier has null llm_source. test_fix_proposer.py: _safe_error_text; repr/model_dump/model_dump_json mask; override reaches complete with exact provider/model/key and usage row is request + key_ref; partial override falls back per field with env/null; no override is env/null; permanent failure (AuthenticationError with the key in the message) keeps permanent=true, persisted error starts with the type and contains [redacted], last_error via API redacted; transient failure (RateLimitError) permanent=false; bad-output path with a key in play. Each secrecy test dumps every table, caplog at DEBUG, and the report/analyses/fix_proposals/queue/usage bodies and asserts the sentinel is absent. test_usage.py: distinct key_refs round-trip through /usage and /usage/{project} with calls/token sums; pre-Phase-7 rows group under nulls; attribution is per project. test_localizer.py: _migrate twice on a seeded legacy DB with project + usage rows.

Not verified here: the PowerShell script runs on BOWIE (documented post-merge human acceptance); the CI workflow has not executed yet (branch not pushed; it runs on the PR).

Design calls made during impl worth a look: (a) llm_source is request only when the override carries at least one of provider/model/key, so llm: {} behaves as no override; (b) the deferred-precondition info log also goes through _safe_error_text (uniformity; it fires before any paid call); (c) the token_usage migration is skipped when the table does not exist because the schema script creates it with both columns; (d) _project_row deserializes ingest_config in db so B1 gets a dict from project_get.

Reviewed ac28b094e30062295a408e5cf8634fd9508cb246 against the approved B0 plan. The application changes cover the override flow, sanitized fix errors, additive usage attribution, merged ingest validation, and migrations. Accepted the reported full suite (247 passed, 0 skipped at this commit); focused reviewer verification: uv run pytest -q tests/test_api.py tests/test_fix_proposer.py tests/test_usage.py => 116 passed. Did not rerun the full suite.

Changes required:

1. [P2] scripts/windows/check-service.ps1:53-66 reports the script checkout's HEAD as the deployed commit, without checking the running image or service. With the supported Docker deployment, git pull without docker compose up --build leaves the old image running while this script reports the new commit; -BaseUrl can also target a different service entirely. This cannot establish the B0 service-version acceptance. Separate checkout revision from runtime identity; report a revision tied to the running build/service when available, and explicitly report unknown/unverified when it cannot be established. Update the deployment instructions accordingly and verify the stale-image/different-checkout case cannot claim the new checkout is deployed.

2. [P2] scripts/windows/check-service.ps1:42-49 discards the response body for non-2xx HTTP responses. /health intentionally returns JSON with checks and auth_enabled on HTTP 503 when its database check fails (main.py:149-162). Invoke-WebRequest throws, so this script calls a reachable but unhealthy service UNREACHABLE and omits the diagnostic checks and auth state precisely when they are needed. Preserve and parse HTTP error response bodies, distinguish an HTTP failure from transport failure, and verify a 503 JSON health response prints its status/checks/auth_enabled. Missing auth_enabled on an older service should be reported as unknown/unsupported rather than asserting BUGALIZER_API_KEYS is empty.

3. The approved plan requires CI green on the phase PR. The submission explicitly says the branch has not been pushed and the workflow has never run. After the fixes, push/open the implementation PR and provide the successful CI run for the submitted commit before requesting approval. BOWIE execution itself remains the agreed post-merge human acceptance step; I am not asking to move it before merge.

Small docs follow-up: CLAUDE.md:65-66 still contains test counts (30/30 and 66 tests), despite success criterion 3 saying the file contains none. Remove those remaining counts or explicitly distinguish historical counts in the criterion.

Phase 7 bugalizer-revive (B0), impl r2. Commit f2b011b on phase-7/bugalizer-revive-impl (on top of ac28b09). Full suite: 250 passed, 0 skipped @ f2b011b (3 new tests over r1). PR #2 opened: https://github.com/jblacketter/bugalizer/pull/2. CI on the submitted commit: success, https://github.com/jblacketter/bugalizer/actions/runs/34719841446 (job "pytest (Ubuntu, Python 3.12)", first ever run of the workflow).

1. Runtime identity (was: checkout HEAD reported as deployed). The service now reports `revision` on /health/live and /health. main.py detect_revision(configured, checkout_root): BUGALIZER_GIT_REVISION wins (new config field; Dockerfile ARG GIT_REVISION -> ENV + OCI revision label; compose passes GIT_REVISION build arg), else `git rev-parse HEAD` of the checkout when .git exists (NSSM deploy), else None. runtime_revision() is lru_cached so the value is pinned at process start: a git pull under a running service keeps reporting the old sha until restart. Tests: precedence (configured/trimmed wins with no checkout; no checkout = None; real checkout = 40-char sha), per-process pinning through the endpoint, and both endpoints carry the key.
   scripts/windows/check-service.ps1 rewritten: "checkout" (git HEAD or -ExpectedRevision) and "running" (/health/live revision) printed separately; verdict VERIFIED only when equal, STALE when different (names both shas, says rebuild/restart), UNKNOWN with "deployment of <sha> is NOT verified" when the service reports no revision, NOT VERIFIED on transport failure. It never infers deployed from the checkout. Docs: GIT_REVISION added to the Docker update procedure (a bare git pull is called out as leaving the old image running -> STALE), NSSM restart note, section 6 rewritten around the verdicts.

2. HTTP error bodies (was: non-2xx = UNREACHABLE). Get-Json returns kind ok|http|transport: PowerShell 7 uses -SkipHttpErrorCheck (detected via Get-Command parameters); Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads the body from $_.Exception.Response.GetResponseStream(). A 503 /health prints status, checks and auth_enabled; transport failures print "UNREACHABLE (transport: ...)" and HTTP failures print the code. auth_enabled absent -> "unknown (pre-Phase-7 build, or /health unreachable)", never a claim about BUGALIZER_API_KEYS. Script exits 1 when any problem was printed.
   Verified in a container (mcr.microsoft.com/powershell:mariner-2.0-arm64, PowerShell 7) against a fake service (scratch python http.server) with -ExpectedRevision aaaa...: match -> VERIFIED, RESULT OK, exit 0; stale (service bbbb...) -> STALE naming both shas, exit 1; no revision + no auth_enabled -> UNKNOWN / NOT verified + auth unknown; /health HTTP 503 JSON -> "ready: degraded (HTTP 503)", "checks: database=false ollama=true worker=true", "auth_enabled=false" flagged; connection refused -> every probe "UNREACHABLE (transport: Connection refused ...)" and verdict NOT VERIFIED. Not verified here: the Windows PowerShell 5.1 catch path (no 5.1 runtime on this Mac; BOWIE's run is the first execution of that branch), and the Docker/NSSM probe section (run with -SkipDeployOption in the container).

3. CI: branch pushed, PR #2 open, run 34719841446 green on f2b011b (link above).

4. CLAUDE.md: the two remaining counts (30/30, 66 tests) removed; grep for a digit followed by "tests" or "/30" in README.md and CLAUDE.md is empty.

Also: the three em dashes that r1 left on changed lines (CLAUDE.md status lines, one docstring) replaced; staged added lines contain none.

Reviewed f2b011bd48cb8a6b27c25066e089103e274d380f. The prior findings are addressed: checkout/runtime revisions are separated, HTTP error bodies are handled and missing auth state is unknown, remaining CLAUDE.md counts are removed, and PR #2 is open with successful CI run 34719841446 on this exact head SHA (verified with gh). Accepted the reported full suite of 250 passed, 0 skipped; did not rerun it. The disclosed Windows PowerShell 5.1 and host-probe execution limits remain within the agreed post-merge BOWIE acceptance.

One new regression must be fixed:

[P1] src/bugalizer/main.py:175: liveness still declares -> dict[str, str], but now returns revision=runtime_revision(), which is intentionally None when no build stamp or checkout exists. FastAPI infers the response schema from that annotation and rejects None, returning HTTP 500 rather than the documented 200 with revision:null. This is the default Docker build without GIT_REVISION and also a supported installed-package deployment; Dockerfile's healthcheck calls this endpoint, so an otherwise healthy service becomes unhealthy.

Reproduced locally without external services or DB writes:
with patch('bugalizer.main.runtime_revision', return_value=None):
    r = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False).get('/health/live')
    # actual: 500 Internal Server Error

Allow a nullable revision in the liveness response type/model. Add an endpoint regression test forcing unknown revision and asserting HTTP 200 with revision:null (also check /health still accepts it). The new test_health_endpoints_report_revision_key only exercises this git checkout's non-null SHA, so it misses this branch. Submit the fix with green CI at the new head.

Phase 7 bugalizer-revive (B0), impl r3. Commit 7b73c30 on phase-7/bugalizer-revive-impl (PR #2). Full suite: 251 passed, 0 skipped @ 7b73c30. CI on the submitted commit: success, https://github.com/jblacketter/bugalizer/actions/runs/34720198795.

[P1] fixed: main.py liveness() is now annotated -> dict[str, object] (same as /health), so a null revision serializes as documented instead of failing FastAPI's inferred response validation with a 500. One-line change.

Regression test test_health_endpoints_return_200_with_null_revision (tests/test_api.py): patches bugalizer.main.runtime_revision to None, uses TestClient(raise_server_exceptions=False), asserts /health/live is 200 with revision null and status ok, and /health is 200 with revision null. Confirmed the test fails against the previous annotation (ran it with the main.py change stashed: 1 failed) and passes with the fix.

No other changes since r2.

Approved B0 implementation at 7b73c30ed74407177b1909fefd2d20af26997610 (PR #2). The remaining P1 is fixed: /health/live now permits a null revision, and the regression test explicitly forces the unknown-revision branch for both health endpoints. Reviewer focused run: uv run pytest -q tests/test_api.py::test_health_endpoints_return_200_with_null_revision => 1 passed. Accepted the submitted full-suite result of 251 passed, 0 skipped; did not rerun the suite. Verified PR #2 head matches the submitted commit and its CI checks are successful (run 34720198795).

All findings from the implementation review are resolved. The documented post-merge BOWIE service check remains the deployment acceptance step, including the Windows PowerShell 5.1 HTTP-error branch and Docker/NSSM probes not executed locally. Approval covers the reviewed implementation; no merge or deployment was performed in this reviewer turn.
